## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A one-juan short Chán treatise, X63 n1219. Parallel recension preserved as gate 5 of the *Shǎoshì liù mén*. Non-commentary; *commentedTextid* omitted.

The text articulates in compressed form the *jiàn xìng* 見性 / *wù xìng* 悟性 ("seeing the nature" / "awakening to the nature") doctrine that becomes the Southern-School signature in the mid-to-late 8th century. Doctrinally the text is somewhat more sophisticated than the *Èrrù sìxíng lùn* ([KR6q0112](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0112)) and probably later: its *wù xìng* vocabulary is specifically characteristic of the mature post-Shénhuì period.

**Abstract**

Scholarly consensus (Yanagida, McRae) places the *Wù xìng lùn* in the post-Shénhuì mid-to-late-8th-century stratum of Bodhidharma-attributed pseudepigraphic literature, slightly earlier than the *Xuè mài lùn* ([KR6q0113](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0113)) but clearly post-dating both the *Èrrù sìxíng lùn* ([KR6q0112](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0112)) and the Northern-School Dūnhuáng materials.

Dating bracket: notBefore 700 (earliest plausible *wù xìng* doctrinal stratum), notAfter 900 (working *terminus ante quem*). Probably mid-to-late 8th century in core composition. Catalog dynasty 梁 reflects the traditional Bodhidharma-attribution.
